chapter: Films, Las Vegas and the union
title: His basses: the Morellis, Mingus's Roth and Uly Apfell
summary: He tells how salesman Uly Apfell sold him the Morelli bass he bought for the Armstrong job, and about the others he owns.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Tell me about your instruments. You mentioned that on your job with Louis Armstrong, you had just gotten one of the basses that you still have. Where did you get it? You also mentioned another time that Mingus willed his bass to you.
Yeah, Mingus willed his bass to me. That was a few years ago, whenever he died...
Almost three years ago, I think.

At least. I got a letter from his estate attorney, and it was a big surprise: "Charles Mingus has willed his Roth bass to one Red Callender." So I went to New York and checked it out, and I brought it back. It was just that simple.
You have that one. You have the one that you played with Louis Armstrong.

I have that one and the one that I played with Louis Armstrong. I got that bass on the 12th of November in 1937, and the next night was the night I opened with Louis Armstrong -- and I still have that same instrument.
Where did you get that instrument?
There was a store on Lower Broadway in Los Angeles at that time called Locky(?) Music. You might have heard of that. I don't think it's in existence any longer.

Yes. But there was a salesman there named Uly Apfell, who for some reason took a liking to me, and he says, "Hey, kid, I've got this Morelli bass from Germany, and I think you should have it." So I went down and got it.
It took me about three years to pay for it. And I still have that one.

I'm going to jump ahead, because this concerns the same person, Uly Apfell. He had his own music store on 9th and Broadway in 1948 or '49. Anyhow, when I came back from Honolulu in 1950, I went to see him, and he had another Morelli, which is a very good instrument, and he said, "I think you should have this one, too" -- and I bought that one.
So I have the two Morellis, and the Roth that Mingus left me, and another little Roblès, a Mexican bass that I have. So I have four basses and five tubas, and I've got a room I can hardly get in!
